text.p: U.S. money leader Phil Mickelson eagled the 18th as he reduced a five-hole deficit to one at the halfway stage of his World Matchplay championship first round against Fiji's Vijay Singh on Thursday.

Mickelson could not live with Singh's opening burst of three birdies in the first seven holes. But he halted his opponent's romp with a birdie at the eighth, won the ninth then birdied the long 17th and eagled the last with an 18-foot putt to remain well in contention for the afternoon round.
"I'm fortune to be close. I couldn't get going until the eighth," Mickelson said.
Fifth seed Colin Montgomerie won the last two holes with birdies to take a one-hole lead over fellow Briton Ian Woosnam.
Seventh seed Mark O'Meara led Japan's Nobuo Serizawa by two holes and Australian eighth seed Steve Elkington, beaten finalist last year, led American Steve Stricker by two.

Mickelson missed the green at the opening hole for bogey, could not match Singh's birdie from four feet at the short second and lost the third as well with another bogey. Then he lost the fifth and seventh, where Singh sank a 35-foot birdie putt.
But Mickelson's 20-footer at the eighth arrested the decline and he won the ninth when Singh bogeyed.

Montgomerie, who beat Woosnam to clinch his fourth successive European Order of Merit title this year, won the opening hole when Woosnam bogeyed but lost the third and did not have his nose in front again until the 18th.
Woosnam is nursing a bad back for which he will have surgery and appeared to be swinging very quickly. But he managed to win the sixth with a 30-foot birdie putt and held on to the last.
He drove out of bounds at the long 17th to take bogey to drop back to level then could only par the 502-yard last as Montgomerie chipped to four feet and holed.
Woosnam said he felt okay but went to the putting green instead of lunch. "I have no feeling on the greens," he said.
Elkington, beaten by Ernie Els in last year's final, was level with Stricker through 11 holes but won the 12th and 13th with birdies.
He lost the 15th sloppily but won the 16th with a 30-footer and both players birdied the last two holes.
"Apart from one back hole I played pretty well," said Elkington, while Stricker felt that nerves affected his start to the match.
O'Meara's clash with Serizawa was similar, the American breaking the deadlock with winning pars at the 15th and 16th before both birdied the last two.
